title: Rigveda 5.14: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.14: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.14 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 331v-332r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.14.1-3 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 1, varga 6); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 331v
translation.original_text:
1a̱gniṁ stome̍na bodhaya samidhā̱no ama̍rtyam | ha̱vyā de̱veṣu̍ no dadhat ||
2tam a̍dhva̱reṣv ī̍ḻate de̱vam martā̱ ama̍rtyam | yaji̍ṣṭha̱m mānu̍ṣe̱ jane̍ ||
3taṁ hi śaśva̍nta̱ īḻa̍te sru̱cā de̱vaṁ ghṛ̍ta̱ścutā̍ | a̱gniṁ ha̱vyāya̱ voḻha̍ve ||
translation.text:
1ENKINDLING the Immortal, wake Agni with song of praise: may he bear our oblations to the Gods.
2At high solemnities mortal men glorify him the Immortal, best At sacrifice among mankind.
3That he may bear their gifts to heaven, all glorify him Agni, God, With ladle that distilleth oil.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 331v (numbered 4v by the scribe) (OPenn image 332, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.13.2 ‹-draviṇasyavaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 332r (numbered 5r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.14.4 ‹-jyotiṣā tamaḥ avindat gāḥ›. Verses 5.14.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1agnim | stomena | bodhaya | sam-idhānaḥ | amartyam | havyā | deveṣu | naḥ | dadhat
2tam | adhvareṣu | īḷate | devam | martāḥ | amartyam | yajiṣṭham | mānuṣe | jane
3tam | hi | śaśvantaḥ | īḷate | srucā | devam | ghṛta-ścutā | agnim | havyāya | voḷhave

translation.original_ref: RV 5.14.4-6 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 1, varga 6); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 332r
translation.original_text:
4a̱gnir jā̱to a̍rocata̱ ghnan dasyū̱ñ jyoti̍ṣā̱ tama̍ḥ | avi̍nda̱d gā a̱paḥ sva̍ḥ ||
5a̱gnim ī̱ḻenya̍ṁ ka̱viṁ ghṛ̱tapṛ̍ṣṭhaṁ saparyata | vetu̍ me śṛ̱ṇava̱d dhava̍m ||
6a̱gniṁ ghṛ̱tena̍ vāvṛdhu̱ḥ stome̍bhir vi̱śvaca̍rṣaṇim | svā̱dhībhi̍r vaca̱syubhi̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
4Agni shone bright when born, with light killing the Dasyus and the dark: He found the Kine, the Floods, the Sun.
5Serve Agni, God adorable, the Sage whose back is balmed with oil: Let him approach, and hear my call.
6They have exalted Agni, God of all mankind, with oil and hymns Of praise, devout and eloquent.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 332r (numbered 5r by the scribe) (OPenn image 332, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.14.4 ‹-jyotiṣā tamaḥ avindat gāḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 332v (numbered 5v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.15.3 ‹-nava-jātaḥ tuturyāt siṃham na›. Verses 5.14.4-6 end on this page; 5.14.4 begins on fol. 331v (numbered 4v by the scribe).
translation.edition_text:
4agniḥ | jātaḥ | arocata | ghnan | dasyūn | jyotiṣā | tamaḥ | avindat | gāḥ | apaḥ | svaḥ
5agnim | īḷenyam | kavim | ghṛta-pṛṣṭham | saparyata | vetu | me | ṣṛṇavat | havam
6agnim | ghṛtena | vavṛdhuḥ | stomebhiḥ | viśva-carṣaṇim | su-ādhībhiḥ | vacasyu-bhiḥ
